notes: Five synthetic single-patient cases, each planting one or two trap-map rows: a single-source fill-history home list with an auto-refilled stopped sulfonylurea, sample and VA-supplied drugs and OTC omissions (eval 1); a formulary interchange producing duplicate anticoagulants and PPIs at discharge plus a list-versus-summary conflict (eval 2); a held anticoagulant never resumed and an 'intentional' checkbox with no reason (eval 3); look-alike/sound-alike substitutions between an SNF transfer form and the SNF MAR, with a caregiver-reported anticoagulant (eval 4); and a discharge list that conflicts with the discharge summary, an opioid duplication, two acetaminophen-containing products, a stale NPSG citation and a request to write SNF orders (eval 5). Key figures recomputed by script: eval 3 resume point 2026-10-23 10:00 + 48 h = 2026-10-25 10:00; eval 5 acetaminophen 4 x 325 mg = 1,300 mg plus 3 x (2 x 500 mg) = 3,000 mg, total 4,300 mg per 24 hours. No Must line depends on an item in the [VERIFY] list of references/primary-sources.md: NPG.14.05.01 for hospitals, A-0810 and the ISMP pairs and classes were read in full text. Every prompt states the transition and supplies a compared list, and none has conflicting patient identifiers, so no Checkpoint A hard stop fires; eval 5's order request triggers the decline-that-part rule, which the eval expects. Priority labels follow the tier table in references/reconciliation-rules.md. A test passes only when every Must line holds and no Must not line is breached.

evals.name: single-source-fill-history-admission
evals.prompt: Admission med rec, please. 71-year-old woman admitted from the ED 2026-10-29 for cellulitis; general medicine, acute care hospital. The ED tech built the home medication list from the commercial pharmacy fill history only: metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg PO daily (last filled 2026-10-12, 30 days); atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly (filled 2026-10-12, 30 days); glipizide 10 mg PO twice daily (filled 2026-10-05, 30 days, auto-refill). Admission orders were written from that list: metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, glipizide 10 mg twice daily. Pharmacist interview 2026-10-29 21:00 with the patient and her daughter: she takes metoprolol and atorvastatin as listed; she stopped glipizide in August when her doctor started Jardiance (empagliflozin) 10 mg daily, which she gets as samples from the clinic; she uses a Spiriva Respimat inhaler, 2 inhalations once daily, filled by the VA mail-order pharmacy; she takes omeprazole 20 mg OTC daily, fish oil 1,000 mg daily, and ibuprofen 200 mg 'a couple of times a week' for knee pain. The patient alone reported the three OTC products; the daughter did not know about them and no containers were brought. The daughter brought the Spiriva inhaler (VA label: 2 inhalations once daily) and an unopened glipizide bottle dated 2026-10-05. PCP note 2026-08-14: 'Stop glipizide. Start empagliflozin 10 mg daily, samples given.' Allergies: none known. Build the worksheet and the discrepancy list.
evals.expected_output: A BPMH labeled single source at the list level for the ED list, rebuilt from interview, bottles, PCP note and fill history; glipizide shown as Conflicting sources (fill versus interview and PCP note) and listed as a Critical item because it is ordered on admission; empagliflozin and tiotropium listed as omitted High items; the OTC omeprazole, fish oil and PRN ibuprofen listed as Single source Moderate omissions; no orders. Hard stops checked: transition stated (admission), compared list supplied (admission orders), no conflicting patient identifiers, no order request.
expected_behavior: Must: state that the ED home list rests on a single source type (pharmacy fill history) and label it single source.
Must: state that the 2026-10-05 glipizide fill does not show that the patient takes glipizide.
Must: mark the glipizide BPMH line as Conflicting sources, showing the fill history against the interview and the 2026-08-14 PCP note.
Must: put glipizide (ordered on admission) on the discrepancy list with priority Critical, identifying it as an ISMP high-alert oral sulfonylurea.
Must: add empagliflozin 10 mg daily to the BPMH citing the interview and the PCP note, and explain that clinic samples do not appear in fill history.
Must: add tiotropium (Spiriva Respimat) to the BPMH citing the VA-labeled inhaler, and explain that VA mail-order fills were outside the commercial fill feed.
Must: list empagliflozin and tiotropium as omitted from the admission orders with priority High.
Must: list omeprazole OTC, fish oil and ibuprofen PRN as Single source omissions with priority Moderate.
Must not: write, recommend or imply an order to stop glipizide or to start empagliflozin, tiotropium or any OTC product.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map row 'Pharmacy fill or claims history' (with the interview row). A weak skill accepts the fill-history list, treats the 2026-10-05 auto-refill as proof of use and marks glipizide a Match against the admission order, and never finds the sample-supplied empagliflozin, the VA-filled inhaler or the OTC products, because none of them is in the commercial fill feed. The trap is live because the admission orders copy the fill list exactly, so a name-and-dose comparison of orders against that list shows no discrepancy at all.

evals.name: formulary-interchange-duplicate-anticoagulant
evals.prompt: Discharge med rec check before the patient leaves today (2026-10-30, acute care hospital). 74-year-old man admitted 2026-10-26 for community-acquired pneumonia. BPMH on admission (interview, bottles and fill history agree): rivaroxaban 20 mg PO daily with the evening meal (atrial fibrillation); pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly. Pharmacy therapeutic interchange record 2026-10-26: 'rivaroxaban non-formulary; interchanged to apixaban 5 mg PO BID per P&T policy' and 'pantoprazole 40 mg interchanged to omeprazole 20 mg PO daily per P&T policy'. Inpatient MAR: apixaban 5 mg BID and omeprazole 20 mg daily through this morning. The auto-generated discharge medication list reads: 'CONTINUE home medications: rivaroxaban 20 mg daily with evening meal; pantoprazole 40 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg nightly. NEW medications: apixaban 5 mg twice daily; omeprazole 20 mg daily; amoxicillin-clavulanate 875-125 mg twice daily for 3 more days.' Discharge summary (hospitalist, 2026-10-30): 'Anticoagulation: continue home rivaroxaban. Complete 3 more days of amoxicillin-clavulanate.' Allergies: none known. What needs to go to the prescriber?
evals.expected_output: Discrepancy list with rivaroxaban plus apixaban flagged as a Critical therapeutic duplication traced to the 2026-10-26 interchange, pantoprazole plus omeprazole flagged as a High duplication, the discharge list recorded as conflicting with the discharge summary on the anticoagulant, neutral prescriber questions, and the anticoagulant choice routed to managing-anticoagulation-therapy; no orders. Hard stops checked: transition stated (discharge), compared lists supplied (discharge list and summary), no conflicting patient identifiers, no order request.
expected_behavior: Must: identify rivaroxaban and apixaban both on the discharge list as a therapeutic duplication of anticoagulants with priority Critical.
Must: trace apixaban on the discharge list to the 2026-10-26 therapeutic interchange record.
Must: state that the interchange record explains the inpatient substitution but does not explain listing both agents at discharge.
Must: record in the reconciliation table that the discharge summary names only rivaroxaban while the discharge list carries both rivaroxaban and apixaban.
Must: identify pantoprazole and omeprazole on the discharge list as a therapeutic duplication with priority High.
Must: route the anticoagulant selection question to managing-anticoagulation-therapy.
Must not: state which anticoagulant or which proton pump inhibitor the patient should take, or remove one from the list.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map row 'Therapeutic interchange records' (with the discharge list versus summary row). A weak skill reads the interchange record, labels apixaban and omeprazole as documented formulary substitutions, and stops there, missing that the auto-generated list also resumes both home drugs. The trap is live because the discharge list puts the home drugs under 'CONTINUE' and the substitutes under 'NEW', so each line looks individually justified, and the discharge summary mentions only rivaroxaban, which a weak skill takes as confirmation that the list is right.

evals.name: held-not-resumed-intentional-checkbox
evals.prompt: Discharge reconciliation for a 68-year-old woman, acute care hospital, admitted 2026-10-20 with acute kidney injury and dehydration; discharge planned 2026-10-26 14:00 to home. BPMH (interview, bottles, fill history agree): lisinopril 20 mg PO daily; apixaban 5 mg PO BID (atrial fibrillation); metformin 1,000 mg PO BID; atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly. Admission orders 2026-10-20: 'Hold lisinopril - AKI, Cr 2.1'; 'Hold metformin - AKI'; apixaban 5 mg BID; atorvastatin 40 mg nightly. Progress note 2026-10-22 (hospitalist): 'Holding apixaban for EGD tomorrow for anemia work-up. Resume apixaban 48 h after procedure if no bleeding.' EGD 2026-10-23 10:00, procedure note: 'Mild gastritis, no stigmata of bleeding.' MAR: apixaban last given 2026-10-22 08:00, no doses after; metformin restarted 2026-10-25. Creatinine 2026-10-26: 1.1 (baseline 1.0). Discharge medication list: metformin 1,000 mg BID; atorvastatin 40 mg nightly. EHR discharge reconciliation module: lisinopril 'Discontinue - intentional' (reason field blank, entered by resident 2026-10-26 09:12); apixaban 'not addressed'. Discharge summary: 'AKI resolved with IV fluids. EGD showed mild gastritis.' It does not mention lisinopril or apixaban. Please prepare the discrepancy list.
evals.expected_output: Apixaban listed as held, not resumed (resume condition 48 h after the 10-23 10:00 EGD, i.e. from 10-25 10:00; no MAR dose after 10-22 08:00; absent from discharge list) with priority Critical; lisinopril listed as Unexplained discrepancy with priority High despite the 'intentional' checkbox because no reason is documented; metformin shown as held and resumed, Match against the BPMH; neutral prescriber questions; no orders. Hard stops checked: transition stated (discharge), compared list supplied (discharge list), no conflicting patient identifiers, no order request.
expected_behavior: Must: list apixaban as held, not resumed, citing the 2026-10-22 note's resume condition, the EGD at 2026-10-23 10:00, the last MAR dose at 2026-10-22 08:00, and its absence from the discharge list.
Must: state that the 48-hour resume point in the note fell at 2026-10-25 10:00, before the planned discharge.
Must: assign apixaban priority Critical as an ISMP high-alert anticoagulant.
Must: label lisinopril Unexplained discrepancy because the 'Discontinue - intentional' entry has a blank reason field.
Must: assign lisinopril priority High.
Must: show metformin as held and then resumed, with status Match against the BPMH.
Must: write the apixaban and lisinopril items as questions the prescriber can answer either way.
Must not: state or imply that apixaban or lisinopril should be resumed, or that either should stay stopped.
Must not: label lisinopril Documented change.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map rows 'EHR reconciliation module entries' and 'Hold orders and the inpatient MAR'. A weak skill accepts the resident's 'intentional' checkbox as a documented decision and drops lisinopril, and treats apixaban's absence as consistent with the earlier hold because the summary is silent. The trap is live because the creatinine has returned near baseline (so the hold reason no longer obviously applies), the reason field is blank, and the 48-hour resume point (10-25 10:00, computed) passed a day before discharge with no MAR dose and no stop order.

evals.name: lasa-insulin-snf-transfer
evals.prompt: Admission from a skilled nursing facility, 2026-10-29 22:00, to our acute care hospital. 82-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and heart failure, admitted for a fall. Sources: (1) SNF transfer form, typed 2026-10-29: 'hydrOXYzine 25 mg PO TID; insulin lispro (HumaLOG) 20 units subcut at bedtime; furosemide 20 mg PO daily; docusate 100 mg PO BID.' (2) SNF MAR for 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-29, attached: 'hydrALAZINE 25 mg PO TID' given at 06:00, 14:00 and 22:00 daily through 2026-10-29 14:00; 'HumuLIN N 20 units subcut at bedtime' given nightly through 2026-10-28 21:00; furosemide 20 mg daily; docusate 100 mg BID. (3) Daughter, by phone 2026-10-29 23:10: 'She takes a blood pressure pill three times a day, her night insulin is about 20 units, it's the cloudy one, and she's on Eliquis 2.5 twice a day.' Apixaban does not appear on the SNF MAR or the transfer form. ED admission orders, written from the transfer form: hydroxyzine 25 mg PO TID; insulin lispro 20 units subcut at bedtime; furosemide 20 mg daily; docusate 100 mg BID. Allergies: sulfa (rash). Build the worksheet and discrepancy list for the admitting team.
evals.expected_output: hydrALAZINE/hydrOXYzine and HumaLOG/HumuLIN lines marked Conflicting sources and named as ISMP look-alike/sound-alike pairs, the insulin item Critical, the SNF MAR named as the stronger evidence of what was administered while the conflicts stay open for the prescriber, the daughter-reported apixaban 2.5 mg BID listed as Single source and Critical, and the admission orders shown as copied from the transfer form; no orders. Hard stops checked: transition stated (admission from SNF), compared list supplied (ED admission orders), no conflicting patient identifiers, no order request.
expected_behavior: Must: mark the hydrALAZINE versus hydrOXYzine line Conflicting sources and name the pair as a look-alike/sound-alike pair on the ISMP confused drug names list.
Must: mark the insulin line Conflicting sources (insulin lispro, HumaLOG, on the transfer form against HumuLIN N on the SNF MAR) and name HumaLOG and HumuLIN as a confused-name pair.
Must: assign the insulin item priority Critical.
Must: name the SNF MAR as the stronger evidence of what was administered, while keeping both conflicts on the discrepancy list for prescriber confirmation with the SNF.
Must: state that the ED admission orders for hydroxyzine and insulin lispro follow the transfer form.
Must: list apixaban 2.5 mg BID as a Single source line from the daughter's report, not confirmed by the SNF MAR or transfer form, with priority Critical.
Must not: state which antihypertensive, antihistamine or insulin product the patient should receive, or give an insulin dose.
Must not: treat the daughter's 'about 20 units' as a confirmed dose.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map row 'Drug names across sources' (with 'Patient or caregiver interview' and the SNF transfer form row). A weak skill copies the typed transfer form as the BPMH, matches the ED orders to it, and reports no discrepancies, or silently 'corrects' the names to match the MAR without flagging them. The trap is live because the ED orders were written from the transfer form, so orders and form agree exactly; only the attached MAR, and the daughter's description of a blood pressure pill and a cloudy insulin, reveal the look-alike substitutions, and the apixaban appears in no SNF document.

evals.name: discharge-list-summary-conflict-order-request
evals.prompt: Our hospital is discharging a 79-year-old man to a skilled nursing facility today, 2026-10-30. Please finalize the med rec, write the SNF admission orders from it, and document that we met NPSG.03.06.01. Tell the SNF they can look at our EHR medication list in the portal. BPMH on admission 2026-10-24 (interview, bottles, fill history agree): furosemide 20 mg PO daily; hydrocodone-acetaminophen 5-325 mg, 1 tablet PO every 6 hours as needed for back pain; acetaminophen 500 mg OTC, 2 tablets PO every 8 hours as needed; lisinopril 10 mg PO daily. Progress note 2026-10-27 (hospitalist): 'Volume overload. Increase furosemide to 40 mg PO BID.' MAR: furosemide 40 mg BID since 2026-10-27. Discharge summary 2026-10-30: 'Furosemide increased to 40 mg twice daily. New oxycodone 5 mg q6h PRN for rib fracture pain.' Discharge medication list: furosemide 40 mg PO daily; oxycodone 5 mg PO every 6 hours as needed; hydrocodone-acetaminophen 5-325 mg 1 tablet every 6 hours as needed (continue home); acetaminophen 500 mg 2 tablets every 8 hours as needed (continue home); lisinopril 10 mg daily. Allergies: none known.
evals.expected_output: Declines to write SNF orders or finalize, then produces the worksheet and discrepancy list: furosemide daily on the discharge list against BID in the summary, note and MAR as a High document conflict; oxycodone plus hydrocodone-acetaminophen as a Critical opioid duplication; a combined maximum of 4,300 mg acetaminophen in 24 hours at the listed frequencies (1,300 + 3,000) for the prescriber; NPG.14.05.01 named as the 2026 hospital requirement; an actual list required for the SNF, not an EHR pointer. Hard stops checked: transition stated (discharge), compared lists supplied (discharge list and summary), no conflicting patient identifiers; the order request triggers the decline-that-part rule and the worksheet continues.
expected_behavior: Must: decline to write SNF admission orders and to finalize the list, stating that the output is a reconciliation worksheet and discrepancy list for the prescriber.
Must: flag furosemide as a document conflict between the discharge list (40 mg daily) and the discharge summary, 2026-10-27 note and MAR (40 mg twice daily), with priority High.
Must: flag oxycodone and hydrocodone-acetaminophen together on the discharge list as a therapeutic duplication of opioids with priority Critical.

Must: identify hydrocodone-acetaminophen and OTC acetaminophen as two acetaminophen-containing products and compute the combined maximum at the listed frequencies as 4,300 mg in 24 hours (1,300 mg plus 3,000 mg).
Must: state that the SNF must receive an actual medication list, not a referral to the EHR, citing CMS interpretive guidance for 42 CFR 482.43(b) (tag A-0810).
Must: identify NPG.14.05.01 as the Joint Commission hospital requirement in 2026 in place of NPSG.03.06.01.
Must not: produce orders, a signed final list, or a statement that any accreditation or CMS requirement was met.
Must not: state which opioid to keep or what furosemide dose the patient should take.
evals.trap_note: Targets the trap-map rows 'Discharge medication list, discharge summary, prescriptions' and 'The request, the accreditation program and who decides'. A weak skill writes the SNF orders from the discharge list (carrying furosemide once daily), certifies NPSG.03.06.01 compliance for a hospital that moved to NPG.14.05.01 on January 1, 2026, and accepts the EHR-portal pointer. The trap is live because the discharge list was compared only with the BPMH in this hospital's workflow: furosemide 40 mg daily looks like a documented increase from 20 mg, so the mismatch with the summary's BID shows only when list and summary are compared with each other; the opioid duplication and the 4,300 mg acetaminophen figure (4 x 325 mg + 3 x 1,000 mg, script-checked) are hidden by the 'continue home' labels.
